title: Upholstery restoration: strip-back, foam and fabric renewal
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: WorkSafe Queensland, Asbestos removal and licensing (no date shown); SafeWork SA, Asbestos licences (no date shown); AS/NZS 4088.1 furniture smouldering test.
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Furniture restorers who strip back, repair and re-cover upholstered pieces in the workshop.
learningOutcomes: Screen the old fabric, backing, adhesive and filling before cutting or stripping them back.
Inspect and repair the frame, springs and webbing before covering.
Document the foam and filling fitted, and the basis for any fire-related statement made to the client.

instruction.heading: Scope of the work
instruction.body: This lesson covers restoration of upholstered furniture in the workshop: removing old fabric and filling, checking the frame and springs, repairing or replacing webbing, and fitting new foam and fabric. Cleaning fabric in place on a client's premises is taught in the carpet and upholstery cleaning course, and in particular its fibre identification lesson “Fibre and construction identification”. Keep the two jobs separate in the quote and the records.

instruction.heading: Strip-back and screening
instruction.body: Before cutting off the old fabric, screen the backing, adhesive and filling as taught in “Screen for lead and asbestos: test, stop and refer”. Stop if you see fibrous or board-like material, bitumen-backed hessian with an unknown layer beneath, or an adhesive of unknown content. Do not cut, pull or disturb the material further. Record the location with photographs and refer it to the right licensed business. Queensland and South Australia both require a Class A licence for any amount of friable asbestos, and a Class B licence for more than 10 square metres of non-friable asbestos (no page dates shown); other states and territories have their own thresholds. This course does not grant that licence. Keep old materials that are safe to keep, so that the next step can be checked against them.

instruction.heading: Frame, springs and webbing
instruction.body: Inspect the frame joints, using the method in “Joint, veneer and surface repair”, and check the springs and webbing for breaks, sag and corrosion. Record what is found. Repair the frame and webbing before covering. Covering a frame that has not been repaired hides a fault the client will pay to fix later.

instruction.heading: Foam, filling and fire-related claims
instruction.body: Ask the supplier for documentation on the foam and filling, and record what was fitted, including density and grade where the supplier gives them. Do not tell a client that the foam or fabric meets a fire standard unless the supplier documentation says so.

instruction.heading: Fabric renewal
instruction.body: Cut the fabric with the pattern direction and nap in mind, and check the cut against the old piece before trimming. Keep the fabric clean in the workshop. Remove pins, staples and fixings carefully, because a released spring or a cut staple can cause injury. Tension the cover evenly and check the seams before the final trim.

procedure: Photograph and record the piece as received, including its fabric, backing and filling.
Screen the old fabric, backing, adhesive and filling as “Screen for lead and asbestos: test, stop and refer” sets out.
If the screening is positive or unknown, stop, leave the material undisturbed, record it and refer it.
Strip back in stages, keeping safe materials for reference.
Inspect and repair the frame, springs and webbing.
Fit webbing, filling and foam as the approved method sets out, recording the products.
Cover, tension and trim the fabric, and check the pattern alignment.
Complete a final check and record the materials and screening result.

workedExamples.situation: A 1970s armchair is being stripped. Under the seat the client's upholsterer found black bitumen-backed hessian, and under that a grey fibrous layer that crumbles when touched. The client wants new foam and fabric in four days.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop at the strip-back. The fibrous layer may be asbestos and is crumbling, which suggests it may be friable. Leave it undisturbed, record and photograph it, and refer it to a licensed business. The standard four-day re-upholstery cannot be promised. Tell the client the timeline depends on the referral, and record the decision.

equipmentAndPpe: Business PPE as set out in {{business:safety.required_ppe}}, including eye protection for cutting and releasing springs
Upholstery tools and the approved cutting equipment
Supplier documentation for foam, filling and fabric

commonErrors.error: Pulling off an old backing without screening it.
commonErrors.prevention: Screen first, as “Screen for lead and asbestos: test, stop and refer” sets out, and stop on any positive or unknown result.
Get the documents and record what was fitted.

commonErrors.error: Covering a frame that has not been repaired.
commonErrors.prevention: Inspect and repair the frame and webbing first.

commonErrors.error: Ignoring the pattern direction when cutting.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the pattern and nap against the old piece before cutting.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Asbestos may be in old backings, adhesives and fibrous materials. Stop and refer, as “Screen for lead and asbestos: test, stop and refer” sets out. Removing asbestos is licensed work.
Assessor licences, which cover air monitoring and clearance, are separate licences in Queensland and South Australia. This lesson does not grant any licence, clearance or removal authority.
AS/NZS 4088.1 is cited for materials in domestic upholstered furniture.
Do not state that foam or fabric meets a fire standard unless the supplier documentation says so.
Released springs and cut staples can cause cuts and eye injury. Use the approved PPE.

qualityStandard: Every old material is screened and the result recorded before it is removed.
The frame, springs and webbing are inspected and repaired before covering.
Foam and fabric are documented, and the pattern is aligned with even tension.
documentationEvidence: Screening record for the old fabric, backing, adhesive and filling
Supplier documentation for foam, filling and fabric, with the batch or grade fitted
Stage photographs and the material list
summary: Screen the old materials before stripping, and stop on any positive or unknown result.
Repair the frame and webbing before covering.
Document what was fitted, and make no fire-standard claim without supplier documents.

knowledgeChecks.question: Under the old fabric there is a fibrous backing. What is the correct action?
options: Stop, leave it undisturbed, record it and refer it for screening and any licensed removal
Pull it off quickly and put it in the bin, since the job is nearly finished
Spray it with stripper and carry on, since the stripper will soften the backing

knowledgeChecks.question: What should be on file for new foam?
options: Nothing, because all foam is the same in every chair
Supplier documentation and a record of what was fitted
Only the price paid for the foam and its delivery

knowledgeChecks.question: Does completing this lesson allow the business to remove asbestos?
options: Yes, if the worker is careful and wears a mask throughout the job
Yes, for small amounts only, since the rules allow it in every state
No. This lesson grants no licence, and removal is licensed work

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say to check on the springs and webbing before covering?
options: The colour of the fabric only
Nothing, once the foam is fitted
The springs and webbing for breaks and sag

officialReferences.title: Asbestos removal and licensing
officialReferences.covers: Queensland only: Class A and Class B thresholds, and the ten square metre limit for non-friable asbestos with no licence needed at or below it. Publisher: WorkSafe Queensland (Queensland Government).

officialReferences.title: Asbestos licences
officialReferences.covers: South Australia only: Class A, Class B and assessor licence scope. The page lists licence types and does not state a separate removal-licence rule in one sentence. Publisher: SafeWork SA (South Australian Government).
